from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Bernoulli Trials", ["A Bernoulli trial has two outcomes.", "Success happens with probability p.", "Failure occurs with 1 minus p."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display Bernoulli Trial definition
        trial_box = Square(side_length=2, color=WHITE)
        trial_label = Text("Bernoulli Trial", font_size=24).next_to(trial_box, UP)
        trial_group = VGroup(trial_box, trial_label)
        self.place_at_grid(trial_group, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(trial_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show success (p)
        success_label = Text("Success (p)", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(success_label, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(success_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show failure (q=1-p)
        failure_label = Text("Failure (1-p)", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(failure_label, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(failure_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Binomial Formula Breakdown", [
            "Formula calculates binomial probability.",
            "C(n,k) counts ways.",
            "p to k is success.",
            "q to n-k is failure.",
            "Formula gives exact likelihood."
        ])
        
        formula = MathTex("P(X=k) = C(n,k) p^k (1-p)^{n-k}")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        comb = formula[0][4:10] # C(n,k)
        rect1 = SurroundingRectangle(comb, color="#00FFFF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect1))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        prob = formula[0][10:12] # p^k
        rect2 = SurroundingRectangle(prob, color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect2))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        comp = formula[0][12:19] # (1-p)^{n-k}
        rect3 = SurroundingRectangle(comp, color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect3))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0.3)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Probability Distributions", [
            "Histograms show probability distribution.", 
            "Parameters p and n shift shape.", 
            "Mean np marks center."
        ])
        
        # --- Create Histogram Elements ---
        # Represent a basic binomial histogram as a VGroup of rectangles
        histogram = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=np.random.rand()*2, width=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.8) for _ in range(8)])
        histogram.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(histogram, "B2", "E5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(histogram), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update colors to indicate parameter changes (p in yellow, n in cyan)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Simulate p shift (color change to yellow)
        self.play(histogram.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Simulate n shift (color change to cyan)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(histogram.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Indicate Mean np with a simple vertical line
        mean_line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*2, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(mean_line, "C3")
        self.play(Create(mean_line))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Quality Control", [
            "Binomial distribution applies in industry.",
            "Use for quality control tasks.",
            "Independence is crucial check."
        ])
        
        # Define objects once
        batch = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(10)])
        batch.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.place_in_area(batch, 'B1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(batch))
        
        # Defect simulation
        defects = [2, 5, 8]
        for idx in defects:
            batch[idx].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(*[Flash(batch[i], color="#FF0000") for i in defects])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        prob_label = MathTex(r"P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}").set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(prob_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        boundary = Rectangle(width=4, height=1, color="#00FF00").set_fill("#00FF00", opacity=0.2)
        status = Text("Accept Batch", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(boundary, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(status, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(boundary), FadeIn(status))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Bernoulli Trials
sections.content: Define the building block: a Bernoulli trial. It is a random experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success (S) or Failure (F), with probabilities p and (1-p) respectively.
sections.example: Visualizing a coin flip: Heads (p=0.5) vs. Tails (1-p=0.5). Imagine a light switch flipping between ON and OFF.

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
sections.content: Introduce the four criteria (BINS): Binary outcomes, Independent trials, Number of trials is fixed, and Probability is constant. Visualize a 'tree diagram' expanding as trials increase.
sections.example: A basketball player shooting 5 free throws. Each shot is a trial; successes are 'baskets' and failures are 'misses', with a fixed 70% accuracy.

sections.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown
sections.content: Explain the formula: P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Break it into components: C(n,k) for combinations (order doesn't matter), p^k for success, and q^(n-k) for failures.
sections.example: Animation showing the paths to achieve exactly 2 baskets in 3 shots: (S,S,F), (S,F,S), (F,S,S). The formula calculates these distinct paths automatically.

sections.title: Visualizing Probability Distributions
sections.content: Use a histogram to show how changing 'p' and 'n' shifts the distribution's shape. Mention Mean (np) and Variance (npq) as the 'center' and 'spread' of the graph.
sections.example: A bar chart showing 10 coin flips. As we increase trials, the histogram begins to resemble a Bell Curve (Normal distribution approximation).

sections.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
sections.content: Summary of when to use the binomial distribution in industry or research. Emphasize checking for 'Independence' as the most common pitfall.
sections.example: A robotic arm on an assembly line: Calculating the probability that exactly 3 out of 10 microchips are defective, given a known defect rate of 2%.
